title: Sylow Subgroup Counting for Order 2024
prompt:
Let G be a group of order 2024. Note that 2024 = 2³ × 11 × 23.

Part 1 — SYLOW 23-SUBGROUP:
Prove that the Sylow 23-subgroup of G is normal (i.e., there is exactly one Sylow 23-subgroup).

Your proof must:
1. State Sylow's third theorem precisely.
2. Compute the possible values of n_{23} (the number of Sylow 23-subgroups) using both the divisibility condition (n_{23} divides 2³ × 11 = 88) and the congruence condition (n_{23} ≡ 1 mod 23).
3. List all divisors of 88 and check which satisfy n_{23} ≡ 1 mod 23.
4. Conclude n_{23} = 1.

Part 2 — SYLOW 11-SUBGROUP:
Determine whether the Sylow 11-subgroup must also be normal in every group of order 2024.

Your analysis must:
1. Compute the possible values of n_{11} using the Sylow conditions: n_{11} divides 2³ × 23 = 184, and n_{11} ≡ 1 mod 11.
2. List all divisors of 184 and identify which satisfy n_{11} ≡ 1 mod 11.
3. If n_{11} = 1 is the only possibility, prove the Sylow 11-subgroup is normal.
4. If other values of n_{11} are possible, you must EITHER:
   a. Prove that those values cannot actually occur (by a counting argument, for example), thereby showing normality, OR
   b. Construct an explicit group of order 2024 where n_{11} ≠ 1, proving normality is not forced.

If you claim a semidirect product exists with n_{11} > 1, you must:
- Specify the groups involved.
- Specify the homomorphism defining the action.
- Verify the resulting group has order 2024.
- Verify the resulting group actually has n_{11} > 1.

Do not assert a semidirect product exists without constructing it.
verification_method: Part 1: The divisors of 88 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 11, 22, 44, 88. Checking mod 23: only 1 ≡ 1 mod 23 (since 88 < 2 × 23 = 46 is false — 88 > 46, so check 1 and any d with d ≡ 1 mod 23: 1 is the only such divisor). So n_{23} = 1. Part 2: Divisors of 184 = 1, 2, 4, 8, 23, 46, 92, 184. Check mod 11: 1 ≡ 1 ✓, 2 no, 4 no, 8 no, 23 ≡ 1 ✓ (23 = 2×11 + 1), 46 ≡ 2 no, 92 ≡ 4 no, 184 ≡ 8 no. So n_{11} ∈ {1, 23}. The model must resolve whether n_{11} = 23 can occur. Since G has a normal Sylow 23-subgroup P_{23}, consider G/P_{23} of order 88 = 8 × 11. In this quotient, n_{11} divides 8 and n_{11} ≡ 1 mod 11, forcing n_{11} = 1 in G/P_{23}. But this doesn't directly force n_{11} = 1 in G. The question requires careful analysis.
why_frontier_hard: Part 1 is mechanical. Part 2 is where models fail. Common errors: (1) concluding n_{11} = 1 just because 1 is a possibility, without ruling out 23, (2) attempting to construct a semidirect product Z_{23} ⋊ Z_{11} but getting the homomorphism wrong (Aut(Z_{23}) = Z_{22}, and 11 does not divide 22, so Z_{23} has no non-trivial action by Z_{11} — this is a trap), (3) confusing the Sylow analysis in G with that in G/P_{23}, (4) constructing invalid semidirect products that don't actually have the claimed order or Sylow structure.
